title: Syndicated Loans and Cross-Border Project Finance
subtitle: Arrange, document and administer large Ethiopian loans with domestic banks, foreign banks and DFIs
summary: Learn how Ethiopian banks share deals that exceed one bank's 25% large-exposure limit and bring in DFIs and foreign lenders, following one cement expansion from the participation decision to signing.
audience: Corporate and project finance officers, syndication and agency staff, credit specialists and legal staff in Ethiopian banks. Entry: Credit Analysis Level 2 or Project Finance Level 1, or equivalent experience.
objectives: Apply the large-exposure, related-party and capital rules to decide whether and how much to lend in a syndication
Win and run a mandate: strategy, information memorandum, due diligence, book-building, allocation and fees
Negotiate the key clauses of an LMA-style facility agreement and intercreditor terms under Ethiopian law
Administer a syndicated loan as agent, from drawdown and interest to waivers and default
Structure cross-border deals with DFIs, export credit agencies and political risk cover within Ethiopia's FX rules and country risk

runningCase.name: Ankober Cement S.C.
runningCase.text: Ankober Cement S.C. (fictional) is a family-controlled cement producer with a 30% foreign strategic shareholder. It plans a Birr 9.0 billion new kiln line funded by Birr 3.0 billion of sponsor equity and a Birr 6.0 billion senior package: a Birr 4.5 billion domestic tranche arranged by Bank A with five other Ethiopian banks, and a USD 10 million tranche (Birr 1.5 billion at the case rate of Birr 150 per USD) from a multilateral DFI called DFI X. You follow the deal from Bank D's participation decision, through the mandate, the facility agreement, intercreditor and agency, to the cross-border structure and the capstone negotiation to signing. All figures are course assumptions.

modules.title: Why banks syndicate: exposure limits, capital and the participation decision
modules.summary: Work out how much of a large Ethiopian deal one bank can and should hold, and why the rest must be shared.
objectives: Apply the SBB/87/2024 large-exposure rules, including connected counterparties, to a proposed ticket
Measure the capital a syndicated share consumes under SBB/95/2025
Explain the roles of arranger, agent, security agent and participant, and what each one owes the others
Decide whether to join a syndication, and at what amount, from an information memorandum and your own headroom

lessons.title: The 25% wall: why one bank cannot do it alone
body: Ethiopian corporate and project needs have outgrown individual bank balance sheets. A cement line, a sugar factory or an aircraft can need Birr 5 to 10 billion of debt, while the large-exposure directive caps what any bank may lend to one counterparty group at 25% of its total capital.

Syndication solves the arithmetic. Several lenders sign one set of terms, each lends its own share, and no lender breaches its limit. It also spreads the credit risk, shares the work of appraisal and monitoring, and lets smaller banks join assets they could never originate on their own.

At Advanced level the question is not only whether the limit is breached. It is how much headroom the bank wants to keep for the client's growing working capital, for its other group companies and for a currency move that inflates any foreign currency exposure.
points: Large exposure: 10% or more of total capital, reported monthly
Hard limit: 25% of total capital per counterparty group
Headroom = 25% limit minus existing group exposure
Prudent hold: usually well inside the legal headroom

visual.caption: Group exposure counts every connected company, on and off balance sheet.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/87/2024, Large exposures
regulation.text: Large exposure means an exposure of 10% or more of the bank's total capital. A bank's exposure to one counterparty or group of connected counterparties may not exceed 25% of its total capital. Large exposures are reported to the NBE monthly within 20 days, and a breach is reported immediately. Exposures to the federal and state governments and their enterprises, government-guaranteed portions, the NBE and intraday interbank exposures are exempt.

example.title: A brewer's bottling line
example.text: Gondar Highland Beverages S.C. asked one bank for Birr 3.2 billion to finance a new bottling line. The bank's total capital was Birr 9 billion, so its group limit was Birr 2.25 billion, and it already lent Birr 700 million to the brewer's distribution company owned by the same family. Its headroom was Birr 1.55 billion. The relationship manager kept the client by offering to arrange a club deal with three other banks, holding Birr 1 billion itself.

lessons.title: Connected counterparties: finding the real group
body: The 25% limit applies to a group of connected counterparties, not to the legal entity that signs the loan. Companies with a common controlling shareholder, or so linked that the failure of one would likely bring down the other, are one risk and one exposure.

In Ethiopian family groups the links are often informal: the same owners, cross-guarantees, shared trucks and warehouses, or one company that buys most of another's output. A participant bank that only counts the borrower can breach the limit without noticing, so the group map in the information memorandum must be tested against the bank's own records and the credit reference bureau report.

Related parties are a separate test. If the borrower is linked to the bank's own shareholders of 2% or more, its directors or managers, SBB/88/2024 adds a 15% single and 35% aggregate limit, arm's length terms and board approval above Birr 15 million.

items.label: Common control
items.text: Same controlling owners or family

items.label: Cross-guarantees
items.text: One company guarantees the other's debt

items.label: Economic dependence
items.text: Main customer, supplier or shared assets

items.label: Off balance sheet
items.text: Guarantees and LCs count toward exposure

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/88/2024, Related party transactions
regulation.text: Exposure to a single related party is limited to 15% of the bank's total capital and to all related parties together to 35%. Related-party transactions must be on arm's length terms, and those above Birr 15 million need board approval.

scenario.title: The logistics sister company
scenario.situation: Your bank is invited to take Birr 800 million in a syndicated loan to Ankober Cement S.C. The information memorandum lists Ankober's own debts, but your records show a Birr 300 million truck loan to Ankober Logistics PLC, owned by the same three shareholders, which hauls most of Ankober's clinker and coal.
scenario.question: How should you treat the truck loan when measuring headroom?
options: Ignore it: it is a different legal entity
Count half of it because the ownership is shared
Add it to Ankober's exposure as one group of connected counterparties
Count it only if Ankober has guaranteed it
scenario.explain: Common control plus economic dependence makes the two companies one risk, so the whole Birr 300 million joins the group exposure. Legal form and the absence of a guarantee do not break the connection.

lessons.title: The capital a ticket consumes
body: A loan also uses capital. Under SBB/95/2025 an unrated corporate exposure carries a 100% risk weight, and the bank must hold total capital of at least 11% of risk-weighted assets, of which Common Equity Tier 1 at least 7%. A Birr 1 billion share in a corporate syndication therefore ties up at least Birr 110 million of total capital.

This is why the price of a ticket matters as much as its size. The margin and fees must give an acceptable return on the capital the share consumes, after expected loss and the cost of funds. A bank close to its minimum ratios may prefer a smaller ticket with a higher fee to a large ticket at a thin margin.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/95/2025, Risk based capital adequacy
regulation.text: Banks must hold Common Equity Tier 1 of at least 7%, Tier 1 of at least 9% and total capital of at least 11% of risk-weighted assets. Under the standardised approach unrated corporates are weighted at 100% and Birr sovereign exposures at 0%.

worked.title: Bank A: capital tied up by a Birr 1,200 million final hold (Birr millions)

rows.label: Final hold in the Ankober syndication
Margin income at 3.0 points over the National Bank Rate, per year
Margin income per Birr of minimum total capital

worked.note: Before costs and expected loss, the margin returns about 27% a year on the minimum capital. The arrangement fee lifts the first-year return further, which is why arrangers compete for mandates.

lessons.tip: Ask treasury and risk for the bank's actual capital ratio and internal buffer before you promise a ticket; the 11% is a floor, not a target.

lessons.title: Club deals in the Ethiopian market
body: Most Ethiopian syndications have been club deals: a small group of domestic banks that know the borrower agree terms together, without a public book-building. The course specification points to club financing among Ethiopian banks for sugar projects, fertiliser imports, the national airline and the telecom operator.

Notice that loans to federal and state enterprises are exempt from the 25% limit, so those clubs were driven mainly by liquidity, foreign currency capacity and risk sharing rather than by the legal cap. For private borrowers such as a cement or steel company, the cap binds, and syndication becomes the only way to fund the deal in Birr.

Two changes widen the market. Banking Business Proclamation No. 1360/2025 provides for foreign banks to enter through subsidiaries, branches or share purchases, and FXD/04/2026 lets banks approve external loans themselves, so mixed clubs of Ethiopian banks, foreign banks and development finance institutions (DFIs) are becoming practical.

left.title: Club deal
items: Each bank does its own appraisal

example.title: A steel mill's four-bank club
example.text: Hawassa Rebar Industries PLC needed Birr 2.8 billion for a rolling mill. None of its four banks could hold more than Birr 900 million within internal limits. They signed one co-financing agreement, shared a single technical consultant and named the bank with the most branches near the plant as agent. Approval took eleven weeks, against the six months the owner had feared.

lessons.tip: Where the borrower is a state enterprise, check whether the exposure is exempt before you treat the 25% limit as the reason to syndicate.

lessons.title: Who does what: arranger, agent, security agent, participant
body: The mandated lead arranger wins the mandate, structures the deal, prepares the information memorandum, invites lenders, negotiates documents and normally takes the largest share. Joint lead arrangers share those tasks and, in a typical Ethiopian bank manual, act jointly and severally as one lead bank.

After signing, the facility agent administers the loan: it collects funds from lenders and disburses them, computes and collects interest and principal and distributes them pro rata, monitors covenants, insurance and collateral, and passes information between borrower and lenders. A security agent holds the security for all lenders where the law allows. Participants do their own credit analysis, fund on time and keep their own records.

items.label: Arranger
items.text: Mandate, structure, information memorandum, invitations, documents

items.label: Facility agent
items.text: Drawdowns, interest, payments, notices, covenant tracking

items.label: Security agent
items.text: Holds and enforces security for all lenders

items.label: Participant
items.text: Own appraisal, funds its share, monitors

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual sets out the lead bank's duties (assess the request, verify the borrower's information, invite participants, negotiate, prepare the co-financing agreement and loan contract, register collateral, disburse, administer and send quarterly follow-up reports), the agent bank's duties (check disbursement, repayment and grace terms, collect and distribute funds, compute interest, monitor collateral, insurance and covenants) and the participant's duties (independent appraisal, timely funding, inspection of the loan account, payment of an administration fee). It requires all syndicated loans to be approved by the bank's most senior management credit committee.

scenario.title: Relying on the arranger
scenario.situation: A participant bank's analyst receives a polished 60-page information memorandum on Ankober Cement from the arranger, with a model showing a minimum DSCR of 1.45. Her manager says the arranger is a large bank and suggests copying its analysis into the credit paper to save time.
scenario.question: What should she do?
options: Run an independent appraisal, test the model and ask the arranger for the data behind it
Copy the analysis, since the arranger carries the main risk
Ask the arranger to guarantee the information
Decline because the memorandum was prepared by the arranger
scenario.explain: Each participant decides on its own analysis; the information memorandum disclaims responsibility for accuracy, and a typical bank manual requires independent appraisal. Arrangers do not guarantee information, and declining for that reason alone would be unreasonable.

lessons.title: Running case: should Bank D join, and for how much?
body: Bank D receives the Ankober Cement information memorandum and an invitation to commit Birr 800 million to the Birr 4.5 billion domestic tranche. The decision has three tests: Is the credit acceptable on our own analysis? How much can we hold within the 25% limit after counting the whole group? How much do we want to hold, given the client's other needs and our appetite for cement and for one family group?

A typical Ethiopian bank manual lists what to weigh before accepting a lead bank's invitation: the loan amount, the liquidity of both banks, the nature of the project, the share offered, the collateral, the risks and the lead bank's experience. Bank D's answer goes into a participation memo to its credit committee, the deliverable of this module's capstone.

worked.title: Bank D: headroom and recommended ticket (Birr millions)

rows.label: Existing: Ankober Cement overdraft and LCs
Group exposure after the deal (23.75% of capital)

worked.note: Bank D cannot accept Birr 800 million. Birr 500 million keeps Birr 100 million for seasonal working capital and leaves the group reported as a large exposure. The memo asks the arranger to reallocate Birr 300 million.

example.title: Saying a smaller yes
example.text: Bank D's chief credit officer, Mekdes Alemu, telephoned the arranger before the committee met. She explained that Bank D liked the credit but could commit only Birr 500 million because of the logistics loan. The arranger moved Birr 100 million to Bank E, which had headroom, and Birr 200 million back to its own underwriting team to place. Telling the arranger early protected Bank D's reputation for the next deal.

scenario.title: Using the full headroom
scenario.situation: Bank D's relationship manager argues that the legal headroom is Birr 600 million, so the bank should commit the full Birr 600 million to maximise fees. Ankober's overdraft usage peaks by about Birr 150 million in the dry season, when construction demand is highest.
scenario.question: What is the best recommendation?
options: Commit Birr 600 million; the limit allows it
Commit Birr 800 million and ask the NBE for an exemption
Decline the deal because the group is already a large exposure
Commit Birr 500 million and keep a buffer for the seasonal overdraft peak
scenario.explain: A Birr 600 million hold would be breached by the seasonal overdraft peak. Holding Birr 500 million keeps the bank inside the limit through the year. There is no exemption for private borrowers, and being a large exposure is a reporting status, not a bar.

takeaways: The 25% large-exposure limit applies to the whole group of connected counterparties, including off-balance-sheet exposure
Legal headroom is a ceiling; the prudent hold keeps room for the client's working capital and other group needs
A syndicated share consumes capital at the corporate risk weight, so price and fees must reward that capital
Federal and state enterprise exposures are exempt from the limit, so their clubs are about liquidity and risk sharing
Every participant appraises the credit itself; the information memorandum is a starting point, not a guarantee

quiz.q: A bank has total capital of Birr 12 billion. At what exposure does a counterparty group become a large exposure under SBB/87/2024?
quiz.explain: Large exposure starts at 10% of total capital: 10% of Birr 12 billion is Birr 1.2 billion.

quiz.q: Same bank, existing group exposure Birr 1.8 billion. What is the legal headroom?
quiz.explain: 25% of Birr 12 billion is Birr 3.0 billion, minus Birr 1.8 billion leaves Birr 1.2 billion.

quiz.q: Which exposure is exempt from the 25% limit?
options: A loan to a listed private brewer
A guarantee for a private importer
A loan to a state-owned enterprise
A loan to the bank's largest depositor
quiz.explain: SBB/87/2024 exempts the federal and state governments and their enterprises.

quiz.q: A Birr 500 million share in an unrated corporate loan needs at least how much total capital under SBB/95/2025?
quiz.explain: 100% risk weight times 11% minimum total capital is Birr 55 million.

quiz.q: Who normally computes interest due and distributes payments to lenders after signing?
quiz.explain: Payment administration is the facility agent's core job.

quiz.q: Which item does a typical Ethiopian bank manual list as a factor when considering a lead bank's invitation?
options: The experience and expertise of the lead bank
The number of the borrower's branches
quiz.explain: The manual lists amount, liquidity, project nature, share, collateral, risks and the lead bank's experience.

modules.title: Arranging the deal: mandate, due diligence, book-building and fees
modules.summary: Win and run a syndication mandate from the pitch to the final allocation, with diligence, pricing and fees that will hold up.
objectives: Compare underwritten, best efforts and club strategies and choose one for an Ethiopian deal
Plan the information memorandum and the due diligence a DFI participant will demand
Build the book, use market flex and allocate commitments fairly
Calculate arrangement, participation, commitment and agency fees and the all-in return to a participant

lessons.title: Pitching for the mandate
body: A mandate letter appoints the arranger and records the main terms, the strategy (underwritten, best efforts or club), the fees, exclusivity and the conditions under which the arranger can walk away. The pitch that wins it shows the borrower three things: a structure that fits its cash flows, a credible list of lenders, and a realistic timetable to signing.

For Ankober Cement, Bank A pitched a Birr 6.0 billion senior package against a Birr 9.0 billion expansion: a Birr 4.5 billion domestic tranche from six Ethiopian banks, and a USD 10 million tranche (Birr 1.5 billion at the case rate of Birr 150 per USD) from a multilateral DFI, called DFI X in this course. Sponsors fund Birr 3.0 billion of equity, one third of cost.

example.title: A mandate won on timing
example.text: Two banks pitched to Ankober's finance director, Dawit Gebremedhin. The rival offered a slightly lower margin, but proposed to wait for an offshore lender. Bank A showed that its domestic club could sign in four months, with the DFI tranche joining by accession when its approvals came through. Ankober chose Bank A because kiln suppliers needed the down payment before the next price list.

worked.title: Ankober Cement expansion: sources and uses (Birr millions)

rows.label: Kiln line, mills and packing plant (imported)
DFI tranche, USD 10 million at Birr 150 per USD

worked.note: Debt to equity is 67:33. The imported equipment is the main foreign currency need, and only part of it is funded by the USD tranche.

lessons.title: Underwritten, best efforts or club
body: In an underwritten deal the arranger commits the full amount and carries the risk that it cannot sell down; it earns a higher fee for that risk. In a best efforts deal the arranger only promises to try, and the loan is signed for what the market will take. In a club deal a known group of banks agrees terms together from the start.

In Ethiopia full underwriting is rare because a single bank seldom has the headroom to hold the whole amount even for a few weeks. Bank A chose a best efforts club for the domestic tranche, with soft commitments from five banks before launch, and avoided underwriting the DFI tranche at all.

left.title: Underwritten
items: Needs headroom for the whole deal

scenario.title: The underwriting request
scenario.situation: Ankober's board asks Bank A to underwrite the whole Birr 4.5 billion domestic tranche so that kiln orders can be placed now. Bank A's group headroom for Ankober is Birr 2.4 billion and its internal appetite is Birr 1.6 billion.
scenario.question: What should Bank A offer?
options: Underwrite Birr 4.5 billion and sell down quickly
Offer a best efforts club, backed by soft commitments, and a smaller bridge within its appetite if needed
Underwrite Birr 4.5 billion through a sister company
scenario.explain: Underwriting Birr 4.5 billion would breach the 25% limit on day one. A club with soft commitments, plus a bridge sized inside the bank's appetite, meets the timing need. Booking the excess in another entity to dodge the limit is not acceptable.

lessons.title: The information memorandum and due diligence
body: The information memorandum describes the borrower, sponsors, project, market, financial model, structure and risks. It is prepared by the arranger from borrower information, carries a disclaimer, and is supported by independent reports so that each participant can do its own work.

Expect five streams of due diligence: technical (an engineer on the process, contractor and budget), legal (permits, land, title to assets, enforceability), insurance (construction all risks, delay in start-up, operating cover), market (cement demand, prices, transport) and environmental and social. DFIs will apply the IFC Performance Standards, and international banks that have adopted the Equator Principles apply them too, so an environmental and social action plan often becomes a condition precedent.

items.label: Technical
items.text: Process, contractor, budget, schedule

items.label: Legal
items.text: Permits, land, title, enforceability

items.label: Insurance
items.text: Construction, delay, operating cover

items.label: Market
items.text: Demand, prices, haulage cost

items.label: Environmental and social
items.text: IFC Performance Standards, community, quarry, dust

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual treats a project loan as finance for new capacity or an expansion that raises installed capacity by more than 40%, requires a feasibility study reviewed before the full loan process, caps tenor at the project life and at 10 years excluding grace and implementation periods unless senior management agrees, and allows principal grace of up to 24 months on long-term loans. Project loans are approved at head office, not at district level.

example.title: The quarry that nearly stopped the deal
example.text: During diligence for a limestone quarry extension, the environmental consultant found that 40 households farmed land inside the new quarry boundary and that compensation had been agreed only orally. DFI X refused to approve until a resettlement plan consistent with its standards was in place. Bank A made the plan and the first compensation payments a condition precedent, and the deal signed six weeks later than planned but with the DFI on board.

lessons.title: Book-building, market flex and allocation
body: After launch the arranger collects commitments and builds the book. If demand is weak, market flex in the mandate letter lets the arranger change agreed terms, usually the margin, fees or tenor within set limits, so the deal still closes. If the book is oversubscribed, the arranger scales back allocations, often favouring banks that bring the borrower other business.

Allocation is a judgment, not arithmetic. A good allocation leaves each lender with a share it can hold, keeps the arranger meaningfully exposed so its interests stay aligned, and avoids a lender so large that it can block votes alone.

worked.title: Ankober domestic tranche: final allocation (Birr millions)

rows.label: Bank A, mandated lead arranger and agent

worked.note: No single lender reaches one third of commitments, so none can block a two-thirds majority vote alone.

scenario.title: Using the flex
scenario.situation: Two weeks after launch Bank A holds commitments of only Birr 3.9 billion against the Birr 4.5 billion target. The mandate letter allows flex of up to 0.5 points on the margin. Two banks say they would commit a further Birr 700 million at a margin 0.25 points higher.
scenario.question: What should the arranger do?
options: Use 0.25 points of the flex for all lenders and close the book
Close at Birr 3.9 billion and let the borrower find the rest
Raise the margin only for the two late banks
Use the full 0.5 points to be safe
scenario.explain: Flex exists for this situation, and a syndicated loan has one margin for all lenders in a tranche. Using only the flex needed protects the borrower's cost; a two-tier margin in one tranche breaks equal treatment.

lessons.title: Pricing and fees
body: Since NBE/INT/13/2026, Ethiopian banks set lending rates freely, under board-approved written criteria. The case prices the domestic tranche at the National Bank Rate plus a 3.0 point margin, reset quarterly, which gives 19.0% at the 16% rate set at the July 2026 MPC meeting.

Around the margin sit the fees: an arrangement fee to the arranger, part of which it passes on as participation fees tiered by ticket size; a commitment fee on undrawn amounts while the borrower draws down; and an annual agency fee. The fee levels in the course case are illustrative assumptions; a typical Ethiopian bank manual sends actual charges to the bank's tariff booklet.

visual.caption: Case assumption: 16.0% + 3.0 points = 19.0%. Fees are paid on top of interest.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest rates (as amended)
regulation.text: Each bank sets its deposit and lending rates freely. Rates must rest on explicit written criteria approved by the board and be reported to the NBE together with monthly weighted average rates. Existing loans keep their contractual terms unless the contract provides otherwise.

worked.title: Ankober domestic tranche: fees (case assumptions, Birr millions)

rows.label: Arrangement fee to Bank A: 1.00% of 4,500
Participation fees at 0.50% for tickets of 800 or more: B 5.00, C 4.00
Participation fees at 0.35% below 800: E 2.10, D 1.75, F 1.40
Commitment fee year 1: 0.50% a year on undrawn, quarterly: 5.625 + 3.75 + 1.875 + 0.625
Bank D's 11.1% share of commitment fees
Agency fee to Bank A, per year

worked.note: Undrawn amounts by quarter were 4,500, 3,000, 1,500 and 500. Bank D's upfront 1.75 spread over an average life of about 5 years adds roughly 0.07 points a year to its 3.0 point margin.

scenario.title: Fees or margin
scenario.situation: Bank F, the smallest lender, asks for a participation fee of 0.50% like Bank B and Bank C, arguing that its Birr 400 million ticket uses a larger share of its capital than Bank B's does.
scenario.question: What is the arranger's best response?
options: Agree, since all lenders should get the same fee
Pay Bank F secretly from the agency fee
Remove Bank F from the deal
Keep the tiers, which are published to all lenders and reward commitment size, and offer Bank F a larger ticket at the higher tier if it wants one
scenario.explain: Tiered fees are a standard, transparent way to reward larger commitments, and the tiers were in the invitation. Side payments break equal information among lenders.

lessons.title: From commitment to signing
body: A commitment letter is only as good as the credit approval behind it. Each Ethiopian participant takes the deal to its own committee; a typical bank manual requires all syndicated loans to go to its most senior management credit committee, and the bank's board where related parties or its own limits require it.

The arranger runs a timetable that lines up these approvals with document negotiation, so that all lenders sign the same agreed form on the same day. Late approvals are the most common reason Ethiopian clubs slip, so the arranger should ask each bank early for its committee calendar.

items.text: Launch, bank meeting, site visit, commitments

items.label: Weeks 9 to 14
items.text: Credit approvals and document negotiation

example.title: The committee that met monthly
example.text: In a 2025 club for a flour mill, one participant's senior credit committee met only once a month and missed the signing date by three weeks, delaying everyone. In the Ankober deal, Bank A's syndication manager, Rahel Tesfaye, collected each bank's committee dates in week 2 and set signing for the week after the last of them.

takeaways: The mandate letter fixes strategy, fees, exclusivity and flex; it is the arranger's contract with the borrower
Ethiopian exposure limits make best efforts clubs more practical than full underwriting
DFI and Equator Principles lenders will apply environmental and social standards, so plan that diligence from day one
Allocation should keep each lender within its appetite and keep the arranger meaningfully exposed
Fees are tiered, transparent and the same for all lenders in a tier; one margin applies to a whole tranche

quiz.q: In which strategy does the arranger carry the risk of being unable to sell down?
quiz.explain: Underwriting commits the arranger to the full amount.

quiz.q: What does market flex usually let the arranger change?
options: Pricing or tenor within agreed limits
quiz.explain: Flex is a pre-agreed right to adjust terms, mainly price, so the deal closes.

quiz.q: Commitment fee 0.5% a year on an average undrawn Birr 2,000 million for one year. Fee?
quiz.explain: 0.5% of Birr 2,000 million is Birr 10 million.

quiz.q: Which standards will a DFI typically apply in environmental and social due diligence?
quiz.explain: DFIs apply the IFC Performance Standards or their own equivalent policies.

quiz.q: Under NBE/INT/13/2026, who sets a bank's lending rates?
options: The bank, under board-approved written criteria
quiz.explain: Rates are free but must follow written criteria approved by the bank's board.

quiz.q: Why should no single lender hold one third or more of commitments?
options: It could not receive participation fees
It could block a two-thirds majority vote alone
quiz.explain: A lender above one third can veto Majority Lender decisions by itself.

modules.title: The facility agreement in depth
modules.summary: Read, negotiate and test the clauses of an LMA-style facility agreement that decide when lenders fund, when they can act and who decides.
objectives: Map a term sheet to the structure of an LMA-style facility agreement
Negotiate conditions precedent, representations and financial covenants that fit an Ethiopian project
Test covenant compliance and identify events of default and their consequences
Apply majority and all-lender voting rules and the transfer clause to real decisions

lessons.title: From term sheet to facility agreement
body: The term sheet summarises the commercial deal in a few pages. The facility agreement turns it into an enforceable contract. Most international and many regional deals follow the Loan Market Association (LMA) recommended forms, which give lenders and lawyers a familiar structure and leave the negotiation to the points that matter.

Ethiopian clubs often use a loan contract between the lead bank and the borrower plus a co-financing agreement among the banks. When a DFI or foreign bank joins, the deal usually moves to an LMA-style agreement with a separate intercreditor agreement and Ethiopian law security documents. Know both and map one to the other.

items.label: The facilities, purpose and conditions of utilisation
Interest, fees, tax gross-up and increased costs
Representations, information undertakings and financial covenants
General undertakings and events of default
Changes to lenders, the agent, sharing and decision making

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires a separate loan participation (co-financing) agreement signed among all the banks in a syndicated loan, gives a participant the right to review the loan contract and inspect administration, and requires that rescheduling, extension or any other amendment of the loan contract be made with the consent of all lending banks.

example.title: Two documents that disagreed
example.text: In a hotel club deal, the loan contract allowed the lead bank to grant six-month payment holidays, while the co-financing agreement required all lenders to consent to any rescheduling. When the hotel asked for relief during a slow season, the lead bank granted it alone and two participants disputed it. The banks spent four months on a dispute that one consistent clause would have avoided.

lessons.title: Conditions precedent: what must be true before the first Birr
body: Conditions precedent (CPs) list what the agent must receive before lenders fund: constitutional documents and board resolutions, signed finance and security documents, legal opinions, evidence that equity has been injected, permits and licences, insurance endorsed to lenders, the base case model, and fees paid. Later drawdowns have their own conditions, such as an engineer's certificate of progress.

For a cross-border deal add the FX items: the bank's approval and registration of the external loan under the FX directive as amended by FXD/04/2026, and any account arrangements the lenders require. For Ankober, DFI X also asked for the environmental and social action plan and the first resettlement payments.

items.label: Corporate
items.text: Memorandum, articles, board and shareholder resolutions

items.label: Security
items.text: Mortgage and pledge registered, insurance endorsed

items.label: Equity
items.text: Sponsor equity paid in before or pro rata with debt

items.label: Permits
items.text: Investment licence, land, mining, environmental approvals

items.label: FX
items.text: External loan approved and registered

scenario.title: Equity first or pro rata
scenario.situation: Ankober's sponsors propose that their Birr 3.0 billion equity be injected pro rata with debt as construction proceeds, rather than in full before the first drawdown. They have paid Birr 1.2 billion so far.
scenario.question: Which condition best protects lenders while staying workable?
options: Accept pro rata injection with no further support
Require pro rata injection, backed by an acceptable bank guarantee or blocked account for the unpaid Birr 1.8 billion
Refuse any drawdown until all equity is paid
Waive the equity requirement because the sponsors are well known
scenario.explain: Pro rata funding is common, but lenders need certainty that the remaining equity will arrive; a guarantee or blocked funds gives that. Full equity first is safest but often delays the project, and a waiver removes the cushion entirely.

lessons.title: Representations: the facts lenders rely on
body: Representations are statements of fact the borrower makes at signing and repeats at each drawdown and interest date: it is duly incorporated, the documents are binding, no default is continuing, its financial statements are true, it holds all permits, there is no material litigation, and the information memorandum was accurate when given.

Negotiation is about scope and qualification. Borrowers seek materiality and knowledge qualifiers; lenders resist them on core points such as capacity, authority and binding obligations. A false representation is an event of default, so each one must be something the borrower can actually check.
points: Repeated representations: no default, true information, permits in force
Qualifiers acceptable on litigation and environment, not on authority
Information memorandum representation covers the facts the borrower supplied

scenario.title: The land representation
scenario.situation: Ankober wants the representation that it holds all land rights for the new quarry to be qualified by "to the best of its knowledge", because one parcel is still being transferred by the regional land office.
scenario.question: What is the better lender position?
options: Accept the qualifier for the whole representation
Ask the regional land office to sign the agreement
Keep the representation unqualified, carve out the named parcel and make its transfer a condition of the drawdown that funds the quarry
scenario.explain: A specific carve-out with a linked condition gives the borrower relief on the known gap without weakening the general representation. A blanket knowledge qualifier would cover unknown problems too.

lessons.title: Financial covenants and the lock-up
body: Financial covenants turn the base case into tests. For a project like Ankober the usual set is a minimum debt service coverage ratio (DSCR), a maximum net debt to EBITDA, and often a minimum loan life coverage ratio. Each is tested on a set date from figures in a compliance certificate signed by the borrower.

Good drafting uses two levels. A distribution lock-up level, above the default level, stops dividends and shareholder loan payments early, while the default level triggers lender remedies. The gap between them is the lenders' early warning zone.

parts.label: Cash flow available for debt service

visual.caption: Ankober covenants: lock-up below 1.35x, default below 1.20x, net debt to EBITDA at most 3.5x.

worked.title: Ankober year 2 of operations: covenant test (Birr millions)

rows.label: Cash flow available for debt service
Senior debt service due (principal plus interest)

worked.note: Ankober is not in default, but it may not pay its planned dividend. The agent informs lenders and asks for the cause of the shortfall.

example.title: A covenant set from the wrong base
example.text: A beverage company's agreement tested DSCR on the trailing three months. A one-off customs delay in a single quarter pushed DSCR below the default level, though the annual figure was fine. Lenders had to grant a waiver they did not want to discuss. Ankober's agreement tests on a rolling 12 months to avoid this.

lessons.title: Events of default and what lenders can do
body: Events of default include non-payment, covenant breach, false representation, cross-default on other debt, insolvency, loss of key permits, expropriation, and a material adverse change in some deals. Most have grace periods: a few business days for technical non-payment, longer for remediable undertakings.

On an event of default that is continuing, the agent may, and on the instructions of the Majority Lenders must, cancel undrawn commitments, accelerate the loan or put it on demand, and instruct the security agent to enforce. Ethiopian banks must also classify their share under SBB/90/2024; its cross-default rule means problems in one facility can affect the classification of the borrower's other facilities.

items.label: Event occurs
items.text: Borrower must notify the agent

items.label: Grace period runs
items.text: Remediable defaults may be cured

items.label: Agent informs lenders
items.text: Facts, options, voting timetable

items.label: Lenders decide
items.text: Waive, reserve rights, or accelerate

items.label: Enforcement
items.text: Security agent acts on instructions

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/90/2024, Asset classification and provisioning
regulation.text: Loans are classified pass, special mention, substandard, doubtful or loss, with provisions of 1%, 3%, 20%, 50% and 100%. Interest on all non-performing loans stops accruing, the directive includes a cross-default rule, and any shortfall of IFRS impairment against the regulatory provision goes to a regulatory reserve.

scenario.title: Accelerate or reserve rights
scenario.situation: Ankober's DSCR falls to 1.15x after a three-week kiln shutdown. All payments are current, the repair is done and the borrower expects 1.32x next quarter. The covenant default level is 1.20x.
scenario.question: What should the Majority Lenders most likely instruct?
options: Accelerate immediately to protect the security
Grant a waiver for this test date, with conditions such as a lock-up on dividends and a monthly cash report, and reserve rights
Ignore the breach because payments are current
scenario.explain: Acceleration would destroy value for a temporary, explained breach. A conditioned waiver keeps control and the record. Ignoring the breach without a formal waiver risks a later argument that lenders waived their rights by conduct.

lessons.title: Who decides: Majority Lenders, all lenders and transfers
body: Most decisions, such as waivers of covenants and instructions to accelerate, need Majority Lenders, which LMA forms define as lenders holding 66 2/3% or more of total commitments. Fundamental changes are all-lender matters: extending maturity, reducing margin or principal, changing the currency, releasing security and changing the voting thresholds.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires all lenders to consent to rescheduling, extension or amendment, so an Ethiopian participant should insist that those items sit in the all-lender list. Transfers let a lender sell its share by transfer certificate, usually with borrower consent not to be unreasonably withheld and a minimum holding, which gives Ethiopian banks a way to free headroom later.

worked.title: Waiver vote on the domestic tranche (Birr millions of commitments)

rows.label: Votes in favour: A 1,200 + B 1,000 + C 800 + E 600
If B votes against: A + C + E + D
If B and C vote against: A + E + D + F

worked.note: Bank B and Bank C together hold 40%, enough to block any Majority Lender decision. The arranger must keep them informed early.

scenario.title: A margin cut by majority
scenario.situation: Ankober asks to cut the margin from 3.0 to 2.5 points after completion. Banks A, B and C, holding 66.7% of commitments, agree. Bank D and Bank F object.
scenario.question: Under an LMA-style agreement, does the margin cut pass?
options: Yes, 66.7% meets the Majority Lender threshold
No, a margin reduction is an all-lender matter
No, margin changes need NBE approval
scenario.explain: Reducing the margin affects every lender's economics, so it is an all-lender matter in LMA-style forms and should be under Ethiopian banks' own policies too.

takeaways: The term sheet sets the deal; the facility agreement and co-financing or intercreditor terms decide what happens when things change
Conditions precedent should cover equity, permits, security, insurance and FX approval before money moves
Covenants work best with a lock-up level above the default level, tested on a rolling 12 months
Majority Lenders decide most matters; maturity, margin, principal and security release need all lenders
Ethiopian participants should align the agreement's all-lender list with their own manual's consent rules

quiz.q: CFADS Birr 900 million, senior debt service Birr 750 million. DSCR?
Which is normally an all-lender matter?
quiz.explain: Maturity extensions change every lender's risk, so all must agree.

quiz.q: Commitments total Birr 6,000 million. What do Majority Lenders need at 66 2/3%?
quiz.explain: Two thirds of Birr 6,000 million is Birr 4,000 million.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a distribution lock-up?
options: To stop dividends early, before a default
quiz.explain: Lock-up keeps cash in the project while lenders investigate.

quiz.q: A borrower's statement that it holds all permits, repeated at each drawdown, is a:
quiz.explain: It is a statement of fact lenders rely on: a repeating representation.

quiz.q: Under SBB/90/2024, what provision applies to a loan classified substandard?
quiz.explain: Substandard carries a 20% provision.

modules.title: Intercreditor terms, security and agency administration
modules.summary: Rank and share security among lenders under Ethiopian law, and run the agency from drawdown to default.
objectives: Design intercreditor terms for senior and subordinated debt and for domestic and DFI tranches
Explain how security is taken and shared under Ethiopian law, and its limits
Process drawdowns and compute and distribute interest as agent
Handle waivers, amendments, partial payments and defaults fairly among lenders

lessons.title: Ranking debt: senior, subordinated and pari passu
body: An intercreditor agreement fixes who gets paid first and who controls enforcement. Ankober has three layers: the Birr 4.5 billion domestic tranche and the USD 10 million DFI tranche rank pari passu as senior debt, sharing security pro rata; a Birr 500 million shareholder loan from the sponsors is subordinated and paid only from cash left after senior debt service and reserves.

Key terms are the payment waterfall, standstill periods that stop junior creditors from enforcing for a time, turnover of any amounts junior creditors receive in breach, and instructing group rules that decide which lenders tell the security agent what to do.

items.label: Senior fees and interest, pro rata
Subordinated shareholder loan, if no lock-up

worked.title: Illustrative enforcement: sharing proceeds (Birr millions)

rows.label: Bank D: 11.1% of the domestic tranche share

worked.note: Pari passu means pro rata to amounts outstanding, converted at the agreed rate. Subordination works only if the sponsors cannot be paid before the seniors are whole.

example.title: The shareholder loan that was paid first
example.text: A textile company repaid its owners Birr 120 million of shareholder loans while its syndicated loan was in arrears, because the co-financing agreement said nothing about subordination. The lenders could not recover it. Ankober's sponsors sign a subordination deed, and any payment received in breach must be turned over to the security agent.

lessons.title: Security under Ethiopian law, and its limits
body: Ankober's lenders take a mortgage over the plant buildings, a pledge over imported machinery, security over receivables and bank accounts, and an assignment of insurance proceeds. Movable assets such as machinery, receivables and inventory can be registered in the movable collateral registry under the movable property security rights law (Proclamation No. 1147/2019, reported). Banks may also foreclose mortgaged or pledged property without court action under the special law for banks (Proclamation No. 97/1998 as amended, reported).

The limits matter for syndication. Land is held by use right, not ownership, so lenders take security over buildings and land use rights as the law allows. Lawyers must confirm whether a security agent can hold a mortgage on behalf of other lenders and whether a foreign DFI can benefit from Ethiopian bank foreclosure powers. A common local answer, reflected in a typical bank manual, is that the lead bank registers the collateral for the syndicate under the co-financing agreement.

items.label: Mortgage
items.text: Plant buildings and land use rights

items.label: Movable pledge
items.text: Kiln, mills, vehicles, registered

items.label: Receivables
items.text: Dealer and contractor sales proceeds

items.label: Insurance
items.text: Proceeds assigned, lenders named

items.label: Accounts
items.text: Collection and reserve accounts with the agent

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual makes the lead bank responsible for registering the collateral with the appropriate body, holding proper documentation and administering the whole loan. It values machinery from customs and invoice documents, requires renewed insurance policies endorsed to the bank, and as a policy avoids second-degree mortgages unless there is a clear margin over the first-degree loan.

scenario.title: Who holds the mortgage
scenario.situation: Ethiopian counsel advises that it is unclear whether a security agent can register and enforce a mortgage on behalf of a foreign DFI. DFI X insists on sharing the plant mortgage equally with the domestic banks.
scenario.question: Which structure best meets both needs?
options: Register in Bank A's name as lead bank, with an intercreditor and parallel debt or agency arrangement that obliges Bank A to hold and share proceeds pro rata, backed by a legal opinion
Register the mortgage in Bank A's name only and rely on goodwill
Give DFI X a separate first mortgage over half the plant
Drop the mortgage and rely on the pledge
scenario.explain: A contractual sharing obligation plus a legal opinion gives the DFI pro rata benefit while registration follows local practice. Splitting the plant destroys the value of the security, and goodwill is not enforceable.

lessons.title: Running drawdowns as agent
body: A drawdown starts with a utilisation request from the borrower a set number of days before the funding date. The agent checks that conditions are met, no default is continuing and the representations are true, then tells each lender its pro rata share. Lenders pay the agent on the funding date, and the agent pays the borrower or, for imported equipment, the supplier directly.

A typical Ethiopian bank manual allows a participant to charge interest if the lead bank holds its funds beyond the agreed disbursement date, and the LMA forms say a lender's obligations are several: if Bank F fails to fund, the others are not obliged to cover it. The agent must report a defaulting lender at once.

items.label: Day minus 5
items.text: Borrower sends utilisation request and engineer's certificate

items.label: Day minus 4
items.text: Agent checks conditions and notifies each lender of its share

items.label: Day 0, morning
items.text: Lenders fund the agent's account

items.label: Day 0, afternoon
items.text: Agent pays supplier or borrower and confirms to all

scenario.title: The missing engineer's certificate
scenario.situation: Ankober submits a Birr 900 million utilisation request for civil works. The lenders' engineer has certified only Birr 700 million of completed work, and the finance director asks Bank A as agent to release the full amount because the contractor is threatening to stop.
scenario.question: What should the agent do?
options: Release Birr 900 million to keep the project moving
Release Birr 700 million as certified and tell the lenders; any more needs a lender decision
Lend Birr 200 million from Bank A's own balance sheet
scenario.explain: The agent acts within the agreement: it can fund only what the conditions support. Paying more without the lenders' consent would expose the agent to claims, and refusing the certified amount would punish the borrower without cause.

lessons.title: Computing interest and distributing payments
body: The agent sets the rate for each interest period, computes interest on the days elapsed, notifies the borrower and lenders, and distributes what it receives pro rata. Day count conventions matter: Ethiopian Birr loans commonly use actual days over 365, while USD loans often use actual over 360. The agreement must say which.

If the borrower pays less than is due, the agent applies the money in the order the agreement sets, usually agent costs, then fees, then interest, then principal, and shares each layer pro rata. A sharing clause makes any lender that recovers more than its share, for example by set-off against the borrower's deposits, pass the excess to the agent for redistribution.

worked.title: Interest for one 91-day period, domestic tranche (Birr millions)

rows.label: Bank D's share of outstanding (1/9 of 4,000)
Borrower pays only 150.00; Bank D receives 150.00 x 1/9
Interest still due to all lenders

worked.note: The shortfall is a payment default after the grace period. The agent tells all lenders the same day.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), unnamed
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual makes the agent bank responsible for computing interest and principal due, collecting them from the borrower and distributing them to the lenders, evaluating compliance with the covenants and informing participants when necessary, and collecting periodic reports from the borrower for all participants. The lead bank sends participants quarterly loan administration, project follow-up and visit reports.

example.title: Set-off that had to be shared
example.text: When a borrower in a three-bank club missed an instalment, one participant debited Birr 40 million from the borrower's current account with it and kept the money. The sharing clause required it to pay the Birr 40 million to the agent, which redistributed it pro rata. Without the clause the bank with the deposits would have been repaid ahead of the others.

lessons.title: Waivers, amendments and monitoring
body: Monitoring is the agent's daily work: compliance certificates, quarterly reports, insurance renewals, collateral revaluations, site visits and covenant tests. The agent is a mechanical role, not a fiduciary adviser; it passes on information and acts on lender instructions, and each lender keeps its own judgment.

When the borrower asks for a waiver or amendment, the agent circulates a request with the facts, the borrower's reasons and a deadline, collects votes, and confirms the outcome. Silence is not consent unless the agreement includes a snooze-you-lose clause, which Ethiopian participants should read carefully.

scenario.title: The late insurance renewal
scenario.situation: The agent notices that the construction all risks policy on Ankober's plant expired nine days ago. The broker says renewal is agreed but the endorsement naming the lenders will take two more weeks.
scenario.question: What should the agent do first?
options: Wait for the endorsement and say nothing
Notify all lenders at once, obtain the broker's written cover note, and ask the borrower to deliver the endorsement by a set date
Buy insurance itself and charge the lenders
scenario.explain: Lenders must know immediately, and a written cover note confirms the risk is covered while the paperwork follows. Declaring default for an administrative lag would be heavy-handed.

lessons.title: Managing a default in a syndicate
body: When a payment default occurs, lenders often form a steering group of the largest lenders, appoint independent advisers and agree a standstill while a viability review is done. A typical Ethiopian bank manual makes the lead bank responsible for negotiating a workout strategy when repayment becomes unsatisfactory.

Each Ethiopian lender classifies and provisions its own share under SBB/90/2024, which can differ between banks only if their facts differ, so the agent should share the same information with all. A lender that wants out may sell its share, but the price will reflect the expected recovery.

worked.title: Bank D: provision if its share becomes substandard (Birr millions)

rows.label: Illustrative provision, before any collateral treatment the directive allows

worked.note: Check the directive's rules on collateral when computing the actual provision; the point is the step change at each grade.

example.title: A steering group that worked
example.text: When a sugar estate's syndicated loan fell into arrears after a poor harvest, the three largest of seven lenders formed a steering group, hired one agronomist and one financial adviser paid by the borrower, and agreed a six-month standstill. All seven lenders received the same reports. The loan was rescheduled with every lender's consent, as their co-financing agreement required, instead of being enforced at a loss.

takeaways: Intercreditor terms decide ranking, the waterfall, standstills, turnover and who instructs enforcement
Ethiopian security law limits, such as land use rights and untested security agency, must be handled by structure and legal opinion
The agent funds only what conditions support and distributes every receipt pro rata
Sharing clauses stop a lender with set-off rights from being repaid ahead of the others
In default, a steering group, equal information and consistent classification keep the syndicate together

quiz.q: Interest on Birr 2,000 million at 18% for 92 days, actual/365?
Senior lenders are owed Birr 4,000 million (domestic 3,000, DFI 1,000) and recover Birr 2,000 million pari passu. DFI's share?
quiz.explain: The DFI holds 25% of senior debt, so it receives 25% of Birr 2,000 million.

quiz.q: A participant set off Birr 30 million from the borrower's deposit. Under a sharing clause it must:
options: Pay it to the agent for pro rata redistribution
Report it to the NBE only
quiz.explain: Sharing ensures equal treatment of lenders.

quiz.q: If one lender fails to fund its share of a drawdown under LMA terms, the other lenders:
options: Are not obliged to cover it
quiz.explain: Lenders' obligations are several, not joint.

quiz.q: What does a standstill in an intercreditor agreement do?
options: Stops junior creditors enforcing for a set period
quiz.explain: Standstills give senior lenders time to manage the default.

quiz.q: Who should negotiate the workout strategy, according to a typical Ethiopian bank manual?
quiz.explain: The manual gives this duty to the lead bank.

modules.title: Cross-border structuring and the syndication capstone
modules.summary: Bring in DFIs, export credit agencies and political risk cover, manage FX and sovereign risk, and negotiate the Ankober deal to signing.
objectives: Explain A/B loans, export credit agency cover and MIGA guarantees and when each fits
Apply the external loan rules of FXD/01/2024 as amended by FXD/04/2026
Stress a mixed-currency structure for currency depreciation and design mitigants
Assess sovereign and transfer risk after Ethiopia's debt restructuring and negotiate a cross-border deal to signing

lessons.title: DFIs and A/B loans
body: Development finance institutions such as IFC, the African Development Bank, Afreximbank and the Trade and Development Bank lend long tenors in hard currency to projects that commercial banks find too long or too risky. They bring their own environmental and social policies, procurement and integrity rules, and a sanctions and anti-corruption process that adds time.

In an A/B loan the DFI is lender of record for the whole loan. It funds the A loan on its own account and sells B loan participations to commercial banks, which benefit from the DFI's standing as a preferred creditor. For Ankober, DFI X lends USD 10 million: USD 4 million A loan and USD 6 million B loan funded by two foreign commercial banks.

right.title: B loan
items: Shares the DFI's preferred creditor umbrella

example.title: Why the B lenders came in
example.text: The two foreign banks in Ankober's B loan would not have lent directly to an Ethiopian cement company after the sovereign default. Through DFI X's B loan they shared its preferred creditor treatment in any future FX allocation, and their country risk departments approved within their existing Ethiopia limits.

scenario.title: The DFI timetable
scenario.situation: DFI X tells Bank A that its board approval will take another four months, after the domestic club is ready to sign. Ankober needs the first kiln payment in six weeks.
scenario.question: What structure keeps the deal moving?
options: Sign the domestic tranche now with an accession mechanism for the DFI tranche and an intercreditor agreement it will accede to
Wait four months for everyone to sign together
Drop the DFI and raise the domestic tranche to Birr 6 billion
Let the DFI join later on different security
scenario.explain: Accession lets the DFI join on agreed terms later without reopening the deal. Moving the whole amount to domestic banks would breach their exposure limits and leave the USD need unmet; different security breaks pari passu treatment.

lessons.title: Export credit agency cover and MIGA guarantees
body: Export credit agencies (ECAs) in the equipment supplier's country insure or guarantee loans that finance their exporters' goods, often covering most of the loan against commercial and political risk. For Ankober's imported kiln line, an ECA-covered supplier or buyer credit is an alternative to part of the USD tranche, at the cost of an insurance premium and the ECA's content and procurement rules.

MIGA, part of the World Bank Group, insures foreign investors and lenders against non-commercial risks: currency inconvertibility and transfer restriction, expropriation, war and civil disturbance, and breach of contract, plus non-honouring of financial obligations by sovereign or state entities. Cover makes a lender more willing to take long Ethiopian risk, but it pays only after defined waiting periods and claims procedures.

items.label: Inconvertibility and transfer
items.text: Birr cannot be converted or sent out

items.label: Expropriation
items.text: Assets or rights taken by the state

items.label: War and civil disturbance
items.text: Damage or interruption from conflict

items.label: Breach of contract
items.text: State party breaks a contract and denies redress

items.label: Non-honouring
items.text: Sovereign or state entity fails to pay

scenario.title: Which cover for which risk
scenario.situation: One of the B lenders says its real worry is not Ankober's credit but that, even if Ankober has the Birr, it may not obtain dollars to pay the USD instalments.
scenario.question: Which instrument addresses that worry most directly?
options: MIGA cover for currency inconvertibility and transfer restriction
scenario.explain: Inconvertibility and transfer cover responds exactly to the risk of Birr that cannot be converted or remitted. The other tools address commercial or physical risks.

lessons.title: External loans and the FX rules
body: FXD/01/2024 sets the framework for external loans, including the 60:40 debt to equity cap for foreign investors, minimum tenors and registration so that debt service can later be remitted. FXD/04/2026 lets banks approve external loans and supplier credits without prior NBE approval, with monthly reporting, and lets banks issue private FX loan guarantees up to 10% of total capital.

For the syndicate this means Bank A's FX desk, not the NBE, now approves and registers Ankober's USD tranche, and its records become the evidence that debt service may be remitted. Check the current consolidated directive before every deal, as the FX rules were amended several times in 2025 and 2026, and confirm whether any offshore account the lenders want is permitted.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024 as amended by No. FXD/04/2026, Foreign exchange
regulation.text: FXD/01/2024 covers external loans and sets a 60:40 debt to equity cap for foreign investors. FXD/04/2026, in force 12 February 2026, lets banks approve dividend and profit remittances, external loans and supplier credits without NBE approval, with monthly reporting to the NBE, and lets banks issue private FX loan guarantees up to 10% of total capital.

worked.title: If the 60:40 cap applied to Ankober's whole debt (Birr millions)

rows.label: Or debt reduction, for example the USD tranche cut to
Equivalent Birr at the case rate of 150

worked.note: The FX desk must confirm whether Ankober, with a 30% foreign shareholder, is caught by the cap and on what base. Settle it before launch, not at the conditions precedent stage.

example.title: Approval that moved to the bank
example.text: Before February 2026, a leather exporter waited months for central bank approval of a USD 5 million loan from a regional trade bank. In 2026 a similar loan for a textile firm was approved and registered by its own bank in under three weeks, with the bank reporting it to the NBE in its monthly return.

lessons.title: Currency mismatch: stressing the USD tranche
body: Ankober earns Birr from cement sales but owes dollars on the DFI tranche and buys imported coal. Under the market-based regime since July 2024 the Birr can move a lot, so lenders must test what a depreciation does to DSCR. The course specification for project finance uses a 30% depreciation as a standard stress.

Mitigants include keeping the USD tranche small relative to Birr cash flow, a USD debt service reserve, export sales that earn dollars, tariff or price indexation where the market allows, and forward cover now that FXD/04/2026 allows banks to offer forward rates. Within the bank, SBB/96/2025 caps the overall open FX position at 18% of Tier 1 capital, which limits how much currency risk the lenders themselves can carry.

worked.title: Year 2 DSCR with a 30% Birr depreciation (Birr millions)

rows.label: Stressed CFADS: 1,560 minus 120 extra imported coal cost

worked.note: The structure fails the stress. Options: a six-month USD reserve of about USD 1.03 million, a smaller USD tranche, or covenant headroom set on the stressed case.

visual.caption: Ankober year 2, case figures from the worked example.

scenario.title: Fixing the failed stress
scenario.situation: The credit committee of Bank C will not approve unless the stressed DSCR is at least 1.20x. Three fixes are on the table: a USD 1.03 million debt service reserve; cutting the USD tranche to USD 6 million and replacing USD 4 million (Birr 600 million) with more domestic debt at 19%; or the same cut replaced by Birr 600 million of extra sponsor equity.
scenario.question: Which answer should the arranger take to Bank C?
options: The reserve, because it fixes the stressed DSCR for good
Cut the USD tranche and replace it with Birr 600 million of extra sponsor equity
Cut the USD tranche and replace it with Birr 600 million of domestic debt
Ask the NBE to guarantee the exchange rate
scenario.explain: Extra equity gives a stressed DSCR of about 1.27x (1,440 / 1,132) and also brings debt to equity to 60:40. Replacing USD debt with Birr debt at 19% leaves it near 1.15x. A reserve covers six months of USD debt service once and does not change the yearly mismatch.

lessons.title: Sovereign risk after the debt restructuring
body: Ethiopia's USD 1 billion Eurobond, issued in 2014 and due in December 2024, missed its December 2023 coupon, and the country's external debt is being restructured under the G20 Common Framework. Foreign lenders read this as country risk: it affects country limits, ratings, the price of political risk cover and their view of future FX availability for private borrowers.

The Ministry of Finance's Public Sector Debt Statistical Bulletin No. 56 reports total public sector debt of USD 52.1 billion at 31 December 2025, of which USD 34.5 billion external, with IDA the largest external creditor. The IMF-supported reform programme and the market-based exchange rate are the other side of the story. A good credit paper states both and then shows how the structure, not optimism, protects lenders.

visual.caption: At 31 December 2025, Public Sector Debt Statistical Bulletin No. 56.

points: Transfer risk: Birr available but dollars not
Mitigants: DFI umbrella, MIGA cover, export earnings, smaller USD debt
PPP projects add the state as counterparty: the PPP Proclamation No. 1076/2018, amended by No. 1283/2023, requires an Ethiopian project company

example.title: Two lenders, one country
example.text: After the missed Eurobond coupon, one foreign bank closed its Ethiopia limit, while another kept lending only through DFI B loans with inconvertibility cover. When Ankober's deal came, the second bank joined in two weeks; the first could not even review it. Structure, not the headline, decided who lent.

scenario.title: Reading the sovereign case
scenario.situation: A B lender's analyst writes that because Ethiopia is restructuring its sovereign debt, Ankober will certainly default on its USD tranche.
scenario.question: What is the most accurate response?
options: Sovereign restructuring raises transfer and FX availability risk, which the structure must address, but Ankober's own cash flow and the mitigants decide its credit
Agree; a sovereign default means every private borrower defaults
Ignore the sovereign position, since Ankober is private
Ask the Ministry of Finance to guarantee the loan
scenario.explain: Country risk and borrower risk are linked but not identical. The structure (preferred creditor umbrella, cover, smaller USD debt) manages the link; ignoring it would be as wrong as treating it as automatic default.

lessons.title: Capstone: the Ankober syndication simulation
body: The capstone runs the specification's simulation. One team is Bank A, arranging a Birr 6 billion equivalent loan for Ankober Cement. Other teams are Banks B to F and DFI X. Each participant team prepares its participation memo from Module 1, the arranger circulates the term sheet, and the teams negotiate the key clauses of Modules 3 and 4 and the cross-border terms of this module until signing.

Expect hard points: the DFI's environmental and social conditions, all-lender matters, the 60:40 question, the stressed DSCR, sharing of security under Ethiopian law and Bank D's smaller ticket. The final product is a signing-ready term sheet and each team's one-page note on what it gave up and why. Assessment follows the specification: simulation 40%, test 30%, a clause review of a real facility agreement 20%, participation 10%.

items.label: Prepare
items.text: Each lender team writes its participation memo

items.label: Launch
items.text: Arranger circulates term sheet and information memorandum

items.label: Negotiate
items.text: CPs, covenants, voting, intercreditor, FX terms

items.label: Approve
items.text: Each team's committee approves its final ticket

items.label: Sign
items.text: Domestic tranche signs; DFI accedes on approval

items.label: Reflect
items.text: What each team gave up and why

worked.title: Ankober: signing-ready package (Birr millions unless stated)

rows.label: Domestic tranche, six banks, NBR + 3.0 points, 10 years incl. 2 years grace
DFI tranche after the stress fix: A loan USD 4m, B loan USD 2m
Total funding and debt to equity
Majority Lenders 66 2/3%; maturity, margin, principal and security release unanimous

worked.note: Domestic debt service stays at Birr 892.5 million. Smaller USD debt and more equity pass the committee's stressed test and settle the 60:40 question.

scenario.title: The last point before signing
scenario.situation: On the night before signing, DFI X asks that its own environmental and social policy breach be an event of default for the whole facility, letting it accelerate alone. The domestic banks are willing to make the action plan a covenant but not to let one lender accelerate everyone.
scenario.question: What compromise is most consistent with syndicated practice?
options: Give DFI X a unilateral right to accelerate the whole loan
Make breach of the action plan an event of default, with acceleration decided by the usual instructing group, and give DFI X a right to cancel or prepay its own tranche for a serious uncured breach
scenario.explain: This respects the DFI's mandate while keeping collective enforcement. One lender accelerating the whole facility would override the voting regime that protects all lenders.

takeaways: A/B loans let commercial banks lend under a DFI's preferred creditor umbrella; accession lets the DFI join after domestic signing
ECA cover suits imported equipment; MIGA covers inconvertibility, transfer, expropriation, conflict and breach of contract
Since FXD/04/2026 banks approve and register external loans themselves, with monthly reporting to the NBE
Stress every USD tranche for a 30% depreciation and fix failures by changing the structure, not the assumption
Sovereign restructuring raises transfer risk; good structures address it rather than ignore or exaggerate it

quiz.q: In an A/B loan, who is lender of record for the B loan?
quiz.explain: The DFI is lender of record for both parts; B lenders hold participations.

quiz.q: USD debt service of USD 3 million rises in Birr from 150 to 195 per USD. Extra Birr cost?
quiz.explain: 3 million x 45 = Birr 135 million.

quiz.q: Under FXD/04/2026, who approves an external loan to an Ethiopian borrower?
options: The borrower's bank, reporting monthly to the NBE
quiz.explain: FXD/04/2026 delegated approval to banks with monthly reporting.

quiz.q: Which risk does MIGA not cover?
quiz.explain: Commercial risk stays with the lenders.

quiz.q: Total cost Birr 5,000 million. Maximum debt under a 60:40 debt to equity cap?
quiz.explain: 60% of Birr 5,000 million is Birr 3,000 million.

quiz.q: Under SBB/96/2025 a bank's overall open FX position may not exceed:
quiz.explain: The cap is plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital at each day's close.

exam.q: Bank X has total capital of Birr 10 billion and lends Birr 1.4 billion to Ras Steel PLC and Birr 350 million to its sister trading company under common control. What is its remaining legal headroom for the group?
exam.explain: 25% of Birr 10 billion is Birr 2.5 billion, minus Birr 1.75 billion of group exposure leaves Birr 750 million.

exam.q: A bank considers a Birr 2 billion share of a club loan to a state-owned enterprise. Which statement is correct?
options: The exposure is exempt from the SBB/87/2024 limit, so the decision rests on appetite, liquidity and FX capacity
State enterprises cannot borrow in syndicates
Only the NBE may lend to them
exam.explain: SBB/87/2024 exempts the federal and state governments and their enterprises.

exam.q: A Birr 800 million ticket in an unrated corporate loan requires minimum CET1 of:
exam.explain: 100% weight x 7% CET1 = Birr 56 million.

exam.q: Which party carries out its own credit analysis and may not rely on the information memorandum alone?
exam.explain: Each lender makes its own credit decision; the memorandum carries a disclaimer.

exam.q: An arrangement fee of 1.2% on Birr 3,000 million, with participation fees of Birr 12 million paid out. What does the arranger keep?
exam.explain: 1.2% x 3,000 = Birr 36 million, less Birr 12 million = Birr 24 million.

exam.q: Demand is short by Birr 400 million and the mandate letter allows margin flex of 0.5 points. Two banks will fill the gap at 0.3 points more. Best action?
options: Pay those two banks 0.3 points more than the others
Flex the margin by 0.3 points for the whole tranche
exam.explain: One margin applies across a tranche, and only the flex needed should be used.

exam.q: Which due diligence stream would address dust and resettlement at a limestone quarry?
exam.explain: Community and environmental impacts are environmental and social diligence.

exam.q: A typical Ethiopian bank manual says rescheduling or extension of a syndicated loan requires:
options: The consent of all lending banks
exam.explain: The manual requires all lenders to consent to amendments.

exam.q: CFADS is Birr 1,320 million and senior debt service Birr 1,100 million. Lock-up is 1.25x and default 1.15x. What follows?
exam.explain: DSCR is 1.20x: below 1.25x lock-up, above 1.15x default.

exam.q: Commitments: A 1,500, B 1,200, C 900, D 600, E 300 (total 4,500). A, C and D vote for a waiver. Does it pass at 66 2/3%?
exam.explain: 1,500 + 900 + 600 = 3,000, which is two thirds of 4,500 and meets the 'or more' threshold.

exam.q: Which change would normally need all lenders?
options: Waiver of a late quarterly report
Approval of a new insurance broker
Instructing the agent to send a reminder
exam.explain: Release of security is a classic all-lender matter.

exam.q: Interest on Birr 3,650 million at 20% for 30 days, actual/365?
exam.explain: 3,650 x 20% x 30 / 365 = Birr 60 million.

exam.q: The borrower pays Birr 90 million of Birr 120 million interest due. A lender holding 20% receives:
exam.explain: The agent distributes pro rata: 20% of Birr 90 million.

exam.q: Enforcement nets Birr 2,400 million; senior debt is Birr 4,800 million split 70:30 domestic to DFI, pari passu. Domestic tranche receives:
exam.explain: 70% of Birr 2,400 million is Birr 1,680 million.

exam.q: Why is a subordination deed with turnover important for a sponsor shareholder loan?
options: It stops sponsors being repaid before senior lenders and makes them hand over any amount received in breach
exam.explain: Without turnover, sponsors can be paid ahead of seniors in practice.

exam.q: The agent receives a Birr 500 million utilisation request but the engineer certifies Birr 380 million. The agent should:
options: Fund Birr 380 million and inform lenders
exam.explain: The agent funds only what the conditions support and reports to lenders.

exam.q: A B lender in an A/B loan benefits mainly from:
exam.explain: B lenders share the DFI's preferred creditor treatment.

exam.q: Annual USD debt service is USD 2.4 million; the rate moves from Birr 150 to Birr 195. Total Birr debt service was Birr 1,000 million and CFADS stays at Birr 1,250 million. New DSCR?
exam.explain: Extra cost 2.4 million x 45 = Birr 108 million; 1,250 / 1,108 = 1.13x.

exam.q: A foreign bank says it will not lend to any Ethiopian borrower until the sovereign restructuring ends. Which structure most directly lets it lend now?
options: A B loan participation under a DFI with inconvertibility and transfer cover
exam.explain: Preferred creditor treatment and transfer cover address country risk directly.

exam.q: Since FXD/04/2026, a bank may issue private FX loan guarantees up to what share of its total capital?
exam.explain: FXD/04/2026 allows private FX loan guarantees up to 10% of total capital.
